page: Amazon Web Services x8i.96xlarge is an eighth-generation memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. The platform is powered by Intel x86_64 processors operating at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. Compute resources comprise 192 dedicated physical cores and 384 vCPUs via two threads per core. System memory reaches 6144.0 GB, which calculates to 16.0 GB of memory per core. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent computational resources across demanding enterprise tasks.

The hardware configuration does not bundle local ephemeral storage, meaning all persistent data and operating systems must be provisioned through external network volumes. Network connectivity is delivered at a baseline bandwidth of 100 Gbps, accommodating high-volume network transfers between external storage systems and other cloud resources. Hardware accelerators are absent, with zero GPUs included in the configuration. The primary architectural tradeoff centers on extreme memory capacity and dedicated compute density in lieu of attached local NVMe drives.

Given its 6 TB memory footprint and high network throughput, the x8i.96xlarge is built for memory-intensive workloads that require large dataset retention in RAM. Common implementations include enterprise-scale in-memory databases, SAP HANA and relational database management systems, large caching tiers, electronic design automation, and real-time big data analytics pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services x8i.96xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance engineered for memory-intensive enterprise workloads. Driven by the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the instance provides 384 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs across 192 physical Intel cores running at 3.9 GHz. It features an extensive 6144 GB memory capacity, yielding an allocation of 16 GB of RAM per core. The instance provides 100 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth to support high-throughput operations, though it includes no local instance storage and relies on external network-attached volumes. With zero hardware GPUs, the x8i.96xlarge prioritizes extreme RAM density and raw CPU core counts over specialized accelerator hardware. This resource balance makes the instance suited for large-scale in-memory databases, enterprise resource planning deployments, massive analytics caches, and distributed data processing pipelines requiring substantial main memory capacity.
